scenario.name: CISA AA23-353A, Mandiant & Microsoft — ALPHV / BlackCat (Sphynx) Rust Ransomware, ExMatter Exfiltration & ESXi/Windows Encryption
scenario.overview: Picture a bustling international airport terminal with glowing departure screens, an X-ray security arch, a boarding gate counter, and a commercial passenger airplane parked right outside on the tarmac. Inside the airport terminal, a disguised passenger approaches the boarding gate carrying an altered boarding pass tucked inside an official airline jacket. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the airport security scanner arch in tiny disguised batches, then smuggles copied records out past the airport security scanner arch in tiny disguised batches. Airfield control tower logs and the boarding-gate manifest counter catch the mismatch when one extra passenger shows up on the jet without a matching ticket purchase. In this scenario (T1048.002, CISA AA23-353A, Mandiant & Microsoft, ALPHV / BlackCat , Sphynx Rust Ransomware, ExMatter Exfiltration & ESXi/Windows Encryption), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: exMatter .NET Data Exfiltration, then access-Token Unpacking , fsutil R2R Symlink, then embedded Impacket PsExec Propagation, ESXi. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering ExMatter .NET Data Exfiltration, then Access-Token Unpacking , fsutil R2R Symlink, then Embedded Impacket PsExec Propagation, ESXi, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 3: Embedded Impacket PsExec Propagation, ESXi VM Kill & AES-CTR/ChaCha20 Encryption
stages.subtitle: Impact (T1486 - Data Encrypted for Impact / T1070.001 - Clear Windows Event Logs)

In this final step inside the airport terminal, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the airport security scanner arch in tiny disguised batches until the boarding pass scanner & tower log catches the mismatch. Under the hood, the observed step executes for /F "tokens=*" %1 in ('wevtutil.exe el') do wevtutil.exe cl "%1" (which invokes the Windows Event Collector CLI utility , wevtutil.exe with the cl , clear-log or el , enum-logs parameter to instruct svchost.exe , EventL so that attempts anti-forensic indicator removal , T1486 during "Embedded Impacket PsExec Propagation, ESXi VM Kill & AES-CTR/ChaCha20 Encryption" by wiping recorded Windows Security, System, PowerShell, or Sysmon audit trails, which immediately causes the OS to write Security EventID 1102 or System EventID 104 and USN_REASON_DATA_TRUNCATION in $UsnJrnl:$J). Next, the follow-up artifact esxcli vm process list && esxcli vm process kill --type=force --world-id=419820 runs (which executes VMware ESXi hypervisor management commands , esxcli vm process list && esxcli vm process kill --type=force --world-id=419820 via the root so that releases exclusive hypervisor locks on Guest VM flat disk files , *-flat.vmdk, *.nvram · T1486 during "Embedded Impacket PsExec Propagation, ESXi VM Kill & AES-CTR/ChaCha20 Encryption" so the ransomware encryptor can overwrite virtual disks at high speed, leaving audit trails in /var/log/shell.log and /var/log/hostd.log). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ bcat_sphynx.exe / ⇠#3 ACK 11) from Node ③ (#3 ExMatter (.NET WebDAV/SFTP Exfiltrator)) to Node ④ (#4 Windows Host (fsutil Symlink + bcat.exe -k)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 SMB Shares & ESXi VMFS Datastores (AES/ChaCha20)).

briefing.plainSummary: In this scenario (T1048.002, CISA AA23-353A, Mandiant & Microsoft, ALPHV / BlackCat , Sphynx Rust Ransomware, ExMatter Exfiltration & ESXi/Windows Encryption), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: exMatter .NET Data Exfiltration, then access-Token Unpacking , fsutil R2R Symlink, then embedded Impacket PsExec Propagation, ESXi. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering ExMatter .NET Data Exfiltration, then Access-Token Unpacking , fsutil R2R Symlink, then Embedded Impacket PsExec Propagation, ESXi, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

steps.plainTitle: Embedded Impacket PsExec Propagation, ESXi VM Kill & AES-CTR/ChaCha20 Encryption
steps.storyAnalogy: Once aboard the parked passenger airplane on the tarmac, the intruder accesses the cabin service locker and redirects flight cargo manifests before takeoff. In this final step inside the airport terminal, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the airport security scanner arch in tiny disguised batches until the boarding pass scanner & tower log catches the mismatch.
steps.simpleExplanation: Using credentials harvested via built-in NetExec/Impacket routines (--propagate), BlackCat spreads across SMB shares, clears all Windows Event Logs via wevtutil.exe cl, kills VMware ESXi virtual machines via esxcli vm process kill --type=force, and encrypts files using hardware-accelerated AES-128-CTR or ChaCha20 with RSA-2048 key wrapping (RECOVER-<ext>-FILES.txt) (logged in Sysmon Event 11 with RansomwareFamily=ALPHV / BlackCat , Sphynx Rust Variant, EncryptionMode=AES-128-CTR , Hardware AES-NI / ChaCha20 + RSA-2048, RansomNote=RECOVER-sphynx-FILES.txt so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes for /F "tokens=*" %1 in ('wevtutil.exe el') do wevtutil.exe cl "%1" (which invokes the Windows Event Collector CLI utility , wevtutil.exe with the cl , clear-log or el , enum-logs parameter to instruct svchost.exe , EventL so that attempts anti-forensic indicator removal , T1486 during "Embedded Impacket PsExec Propagation, ESXi VM Kill & AES-CTR/ChaCha20 Encryption" by wiping recorded Windows Security, System, PowerShell, or Sysmon audit trails, which immediately causes the OS to write Security EventID 1102 or System EventID 104 and USN_REASON_DATA_TRUNCATION in $UsnJrnl:$J). Next, the follow-up artifact esxcli vm process list && esxcli vm process kill --type=force --world-id=419820 runs (which executes VMware ESXi hypervisor management commands , esxcli vm process list && esxcli vm process kill --type=force --world-id=419820 via the root so that releases exclusive hypervisor locks on Guest VM flat disk files , *-flat.vmdk, *.nvram · T1486 during "Embedded Impacket PsExec Propagation, ESXi VM Kill & AES-CTR/ChaCha20 Encryption" so the ransomware encryptor can overwrite virtual disks at high speed, leaving audit trails in /var/log/shell.log and /var/log/hostd.log).

steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in Sysmon Event 11 (recording RansomwareFamily=ALPHV / BlackCat , Sphynx Rust Variant, EncryptionMode=AES-128-CTR , Hardware AES-NI / ChaCha20 + RSA-2048, RansomNote=RECOVER-sphynx-FILES.txt under T1486): Segment ESXi management interfaces onto isolated jump VLANs with MFA, enforce SMB signing, and forward Windows Event Logs in real time prior to wevtutil.exe cl truncation.
